NC500 in 3 Days: The Fast-Track Guide

Three days is tight for the NC500 but absolutely doable on a motorcycle. You'll be covering roughly 170 miles per day, which sounds manageable until you factor in single-track roads, photo stops, and the sheer volume of stunning scenery demanding your attention. Here's how to make it work.

Day 1: Inverness to Durness (170 miles)

Leave Inverness early and head north on the A9 to Lairg, then west on the A838. The east coast section is fast and efficient — save your dawdling for the north coast. Key stops:

  • Dunrobin Castle — Quick photo stop, fairy-tale Scottish castle
  • Smoo Cave, Durness — Arrive with enough daylight to explore this massive sea cave
  • Fuel at Lairg and Tongue — don't skip these

Overnight in Durness. The Mackay's Hotel is biker-friendly with secure parking.

Day 2: Durness to Ullapool (160 miles)

This is the showstopper day. The road from Durness south along the A838 and A894 passes through some of Scotland's wildest landscapes. The Kylesku Bridge is a highlight — stop for photos. Continue south through Lochinver and down to Ullapool.

  • Kylesku Bridge — Stunning curved bridge over a sea loch
  • Knockan Crag — Quick geological viewpoint stop
  • Ullapool — Charming fishing village, perfect overnight stop

Fill up at Lochinver — fuel options are limited on this stretch.

Day 3: Ullapool to Inverness via Applecross (190 miles)

The longest day, but the most rewarding. Head south from Ullapool on the A835, then detour to Applecross via the Bealach na Bà. This pass is the NC500's crown jewel — don't skip it even on a tight schedule. Return to the A87 and head east through Glen Carron back to Inverness.

Three days is the minimum for the NC500 on a motorcycle. You'll see the highlights but miss the hidden gems. If you can stretch to five days, do it — the experience doubles.

Essential Tips for the 3-Day NC500

Start each day by 8am to maximise your riding time. Pre-book all accommodation — there's nothing worse than arriving exhausted with nowhere to stay. Pack light — you need to be efficient with a 3-day schedule. Carry snacks and water, as cafes can be sparse and unpredictably closed. keyTakeaways: Three days means roughly 170 miles per day, tight but achievable on a motorcycle.
Day 1 runs Inverness to Durness via the A9 to Lairg then the A838, taking in Dunrobin Castle and Smoo Cave.
Day 2 is the showstopper south from Durness on the A838 and A894 past Kylesku Bridge to Ullapool.
Day 3 is the longest at 190 miles, including the Bealach na Ba detour to Applecross.
Pre-book accommodation, start by 8am each day and check tyre pressures before departure as the nearest fitter is in Inverness.

faq.q: Is three days enough for the NC500?
faq.a: Three days is the practical minimum on a motorcycle. You will cover roughly 170 miles daily and see the highlights, but you will miss many hidden gems. If you can stretch to five days the experience roughly doubles, giving time for photography, walking and scenic detours.

faq.q: Where should I stop overnight on a 3-day NC500?
faq.a: Durness on night one and Ullapool on night two work well for the mileage. Mackay's Hotel in Durness is biker-friendly with secure parking. Pre-book everything, as arriving exhausted with nowhere to stay is the worst way to end a long Highland day.

faq.q: Which fuel stops matter on the 3-day route?
faq.a: Fuel at Lairg and Tongue on day one, and top up at Lochinver on day two where options are limited on the stretch to Ullapool. On the west coast generally, fill up whenever you can rather than when you must, because remote stations keep short hours.

faq.q: How can I make the tight schedule work?
faq.a: Start each day by 8am to maximise riding time, pack light and pre-book all accommodation. Carry snacks and water as cafes can be sparse and unpredictably closed, and check tyre pressures before departure since the nearest motorcycle tyre fitter is back in Inverness.
